answer: Used Cambridge Dictionary to understand English articles. On https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/a-an-and-the ('A/an and the' under Grammar > Nouns, pronouns and determiners > Determiners): 'a/an' is the indefinite article and 'the' is the definite article. 'A' is used before words beginning with a consonant sound (e.g., 'a car', 'a university') and 'an' before a vowel sound (e.g., 'an apple', 'an hour'). With countable nouns, articles are used with singular forms (e.g., 'I have a sister and a brother.', 'The lion roared.'); 'the' can also be used with plurals when specific. With uncountable nouns, 'a/an' is not used (e.g., 'The rice we bought in the Thai shop is much better than the one we bought in the supermarket.'); uncountable nouns take no article when general and 'the' when specific.
